EXPLANATION: Key bands match a tert-butyl ketone that also contains a methoxy (ether) group.  
• 1707 cm⁻¹ – C=O stretch of a non-conjugated ketone.  
• 1442 cm⁻¹ – CH₃ asymmetric deformation, intense for multiple methyls.  
• 734 cm⁻¹ – very strong CH₃ rocking band typical of a (CH₃)₃C (tert-butyl) group.  
• 1079 cm⁻¹ and 931 cm⁻¹ – strong C–O–C stretching modes characteristic of a methoxy ether; candidate 1 is the only tert-butyl ketone that also contains an O–CH₃ single bond.  
Other candidates with a methoxy group lack the large tert-butyl group (so would not give the dominant 734 cm⁻¹ peak), while the simple tert-butyl ketone (candidate 2) cannot account for the strong 1079 cm⁻¹ C–O stretch.  
Thus COC(C)(C)CC(C)=O (candidate 1) best fits the observed Raman pattern.
